name: WV-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans about 20 points Republican, among the reddest House seats
Incumbent Riley Moore holds a roughly 10-to-1 fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price the Republican near 97 percent
No polls or expert ratings; challenger Ace Parsi is minimally funded
model.rationale: The district's twenty-point Republican lean, Moore's roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge, and prediction markets pricing the Republican near 97 percent all point to a safe hold, and no polling or ratings surface any competitive risk.
model.watch: Only a major late scandal or a sudden wave of outside spending against Moore would put the outcome in any doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
West Virginia's second district is among the most Republican-leaning House seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly twenty points to the right. Riley Moore, the Republican incumbent, is running for a second term after winning the seat in 2024. His Democratic challenger, Ace Parsi, has raised about $134,000 and had roughly $44,000 on hand, while Moore has raised about $1.3 million with $751,000 available. No outside groups have invested meaningfully on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, and prediction markets put the Republican's chances around 97 percent. With that lopsided financial picture, a deeply favorable district, and the advantages of incumbency, the race is rated Safe Republican. The main uncertainty is the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
